title: 哲学经典详解：知识与智慧 · Day 4 — Philosophy
title_en: Philosophy Classics: Knowledge and Wisdom · Day 4 — Philosophy

questions.question: 康德的「哥白尼革命」主张的是什么？
options: 对象符合心智的认识结构而非相反，所以人能确知现象、够不到物自体
认识要尽量符合外部对象，凡与对象不符的观念都应作为偏见被剔除掉
只要观察足够细致、仪器足够精密，人最终就能直接认识事物本身的样子
一切知识都源自经验，心智是一块白板，时间、空间与因果都是从观察中归纳出来的
questions.explanation: 康德把方向反过来：时间、空间和范畴是心智的先天形式，世界经它们过滤后才成为现象。所以现象界能被确知，物自体在结构之外永远够不到。他说一切知识都从经验开始，但并非一切知识都源自经验，白板说正是他要推翻的。
options_en: Not that cognition conforms to objects but that objects conform to the mind's structure, so we can know phenomena but never the thing-in-itself
That cognition should match external objects as closely as possible, discarding any idea that fails to match as prejudice
That with careful enough observation and precise enough instruments, we can eventually know things as they are in themselves
That all knowledge derives from experience; the mind is a blank slate, and space, time and causality are generalized from observation
questions.explanation_en: Kant reversed the direction: space, time and the categories are a priori forms of the mind, and the world becomes phenomena only after passing through them. So phenomena can be known with certainty while the thing-in-itself lies forever outside. He held that all knowledge begins with experience but not all of it arises from experience; the blank slate is what he overturned.

questions.question: 禅宗「不立文字」应当怎样理解？
options: 认为语言能完整表达实相，只是禅师们为了保守秘传才选择不写下来
不否定文字本身，而否定文字的自足性：语言是指月之指，真知要落在直接体验里
主张彻底抛弃经书和语言，因为文字会污染心性，所以修行者不该读经讲经
认为只要把经文读得足够透彻、背得足够熟练，就能自然证悟般若真知
questions.explanation: 「不立文字」不是反智：六祖自己也讲经。它对治的是「我读过它＝我懂得它＝我活出了它」的执念；文字指向月亮，但本身不是月亮，执着于指头就看不到月亮。
questions.question_en: How should the Chan (Zen) principle of "not establishing words" be understood?
options_en: It holds that language can fully express reality, and masters simply chose not to write it down to keep the teaching secret
It doesn't reject words as such but their self-sufficiency: language is a finger pointing at the moon, and real insight lies in direct experience
It calls for abandoning scripture and language altogether, since words defile the mind and practitioners shouldn't read or teach sutras
It holds that reading the sutras thoroughly and memorizing them well enough will by itself bring awakening to wisdom
questions.explanation_en: Not establishing words isn't anti-intellectual; the Sixth Patriarch himself expounded sutras. It targets the conviction that having read something equals understanding it equals living it; words point at the moon but are not the moon, and clinging to the finger means never seeing the moon.

questions.question: 康德说物自体永远不可知，禅宗却说可以「见性」。按文章的分析，两者是什么关系？
options: 完全一致：禅宗的见性就是康德所说的用范畴认识现象，只是换了一套宗教词汇来表达
不是正面冲突：两者都认为概念够不到实相，分歧只在禅宗主张还有一条非概念的直接体证之路
康德驳倒了禅宗：既然物自体不可知，见性只能是一种先验幻象，可以从逻辑上排除
正面冲突：康德认为概念能把握实相，禅宗则认为只有放下概念才能把握，两者必有一错
questions.explanation: 康德封死的是概念之路，禅宗同意语言与概念够不到实相，但主张还有一条放下能所对立的体证之路。所以两者是在同一堵墙前分手：康德证明墙在哪里并守在墙内，禅宗声称墙外有路，那条路无法被论证，只能被走。
questions.question_en: Kant says the thing-in-itself is forever unknowable, yet Chan says one can "see one's nature." On the piece's analysis, how do the two relate?
options_en: They agree entirely: seeing one's nature is just Kant's knowing phenomena through the categories, restated in religious vocabulary
They don't directly clash: both hold that concepts can't reach reality, and differ only in that Chan claims a non-conceptual path of direct realization
Kant refutes Chan: since the thing-in-itself is unknowable, seeing one's nature can only be a transcendental illusion, ruled out by logic
They clash head-on: Kant holds concepts can grasp reality while Chan holds only dropping concepts can, so one of them must be wrong
questions.explanation_en: Kant closes the conceptual road; Chan agrees that language and concepts can't reach reality but claims a path of direct realization beyond the subject-object split. They part ways at the same wall: Kant shows where it stands and works inside it, while Chan claims a path beyond it that can't be argued for, only walked.
